newsitem.title: UK: Oftel says regulation won't delay digital TV.
newsitem.headline: Oftel says regulation won't delay digital TV.

text.p: Oftel said on Thursday that its framing of regulations would not slow the launch of digital television in the UK.
"We will not be a delaying factor...We are conscious that everyone wants to move fast," Oftel Director General Don Cruickshank told a news conference.
Cruickshank was speaking as watchdog Oftel launched a consultative document on the regulation of conditional access services for digital TV.
Satellite broadcaster BSkyB is planning to launch digital services with some 200 channels late next year.
A terrestrial version of digital television is expected to begin in mid-1998, offering 35 or so channels.
Conditional access concerns the control of the scrambling and unscrambling of digital broadcast signals according to whether a viewer has paid for a particular programme or service.
Many media players have voiced concern that BSkyB, as the first entrant into the market, will gain de facto control of the digital world.
Cruickshank agreed with a questioner that there had been a good deal of "misinformation" in the press about the threat of domination by BSkyB.
Outlining Oftel's plans, Cruickshank said that it would seek to ensure that control of conditional access technology was not used to distort, restrict or prevent competition in television.
Oftel will also police the Electronic Programme Guides (EPGs) which viewers will need to navigate around the hundreds of channels in the digital era.
Cruickshank said it would not be easy to regulate these but he was determined to ensure they operated on a fair basis and would seek comments from viewers to make sure this happened.
Some broadcasters fear their channels may be tucked away on a distant programme number while those associated with the conditional access supplier are given the prime slots.
